planner.question: Can exact semantic affine restrictions compress the universal selector's satisfiable region, and do their lower bounds transfer to arbitrary nonlinear circuits?
planner.strategy: Prove affine dimension rigidity, exact pair deficit and exact affine cover number from maximal selector code.
planner.alternative: Characterize local affine certificates for all monotone functions and audit the AND-gate decision-tree simulation.
planner.stop_rule: Do not infer superpolynomial gate complexity from exponential affine cover complexity.
literature_leads: Prior MathOS selector-degree and direct DAG restriction; elementary binary affine linear algebra and inclusion-exclusion. No novelty claim.

construct.claim: The satisfiable selector region has exact affine cover number 2^n, dimension-q rigidity for n>=2 and exact pair-containing dimension q-D(x,y)+1.
construct.scope: Full normalized nonempty width-at-most-three signed clause pool, GF(2) affine flats contained in SAT.
construct.derivation: Information sets bound weight; triple XOR violates a binary clause; graph of a linear map gives pair deficit; volume and small-n arguments give exact cover.
unresolved_steps: A noncircular gate-size transfer from semantic affine structure.
candidate_tests: Enumerate all small satisfiable flats, exact pair maxima, triple obstructions and union cardinalities.

alternative.claim: For every monotone Boolean function local affine certificate codimension equals ordinary coordinate certificate size; exponential affine covers can coexist with linear circuits.
alternative.scope: Exact monochromatic affine flats through an input; XOR-AND circuits with affine operations free; unit-only SAT control.
alternative.derivation: Intersect a constant flat with fixed zero coordinates and select information-set zeros; simulate AND gates by adaptive affine queries; unit-only volume gives exponential cover.
unresolved_steps: Resource-sensitive circuit elimination stronger than degree or cover counting.
candidate_tests: All monotone three-input functions and all affine flats; unit-only cover and gate semantics.
